newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat quality dominates Iraqi tender talks.
newsitem.headline: French wheat quality dominates Iraqi tender talks.

text.p: Wheat quality criteria were the main focus of negotiations between Iraqi officials and grain exporters in a tender for the import of some 100,000 tonnes of French wheat, exporters said on Tuesday.
"Discussions involve specific weight, the Iraqis want wheat with a specific weight of 78 kg while most offers involved a specific weight of 76 kg," one exporter said.
But there was a premium of at least four or five dollars for higher quality wheat with a specific weight of 78 kg when compared to standard quality wheat of a specific weight of 76 kg, they said.

There were no details about the initial bid levels but Iraq made a counter-offer to buy French wheat with a specific weight of 77 kg at $182 per tonne, cost and freight, one exporter close to the talks said.
"That's where we stand for now, we are reviewing our offers on this new basis," he said.
Iraq is seeking about 100,000 tonnes of French wheat for shipment in September and October and 70,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for shipment from October onward.
The deadline for submitting the bids was August 15 with an answer due by August 20.
French grain exporters have said they hope Iraq may end up buying at least 100,000 tonnes of French wheat while there is also talk Iraq may be discussing wheat imports with Canada and Australia.
